channel.title: Fragments of the Universe — Bhapstar Astrophotography
channel.description: Astrophotography from a Dubai balcony and the dark skies of the UAE desert. Deep-sky images, gear notes and guides for anyone starting out under the stars.

image.title: Fragments of the Universe — Bhapstar Astrophotography

item.title: How to Photograph a Meteor Shower
item.description: Which showers are worth staying up for, why you should point away from the radiant rather than at it, and why the trick is taking far more frames than feels sensible. Works with a phone or a camera.

item.title: Imaging Deep Sky from a Bortle 8 Balcony
item.description: Most city astrophotography advice assumes a garden. A balcony takes away your view of Polaris, most of the sky, and half the night. Here is how to work with all three, and why it is still worth doing.

item.title: How I Plan Every Astrophotography Session Using Stellarium
item.description: The software I open before every session. What is up tonight, how high it gets, when it is highest, and whether it will actually fit inside the frame.

item.title: The Bortle Scale of Night-Sky Brightness and Light Pollution
item.description: Why a city sky buries a nebula instead of dimming it, how to score your own sky from one to nine tonight, and what 7nm and 3nm narrowband filters really do about it.

item.title: The Seestar S30 Pro: A Whole Observatory in a Shoulder Bag
item.description: Deep sky and the Milky Way from the same 1.65kg box. Why the dual-lens Pro changed which rig I actually carry, and where a 30mm aperture stops.

item.title: The Rig: A Mount, a Refractor, and a Camera That Runs Itself
item.description: A tour of the setup that takes every deep-sky image on this site. Why the mount has no counterweight, why the camera replaced a laptop, and how the whole thing runs all night on eleven watts.

item.title: Navigating the Night Sky: Polaris, the Poles and the Lines Between Them
item.description: The sky is a giant ball and you are standing in the middle of it. How to find Polaris, why the south has no north star, and what the celestial equator and the meridian actually are.

item.title: How to Photograph the Milky Way with Your Phone
item.description: No camera and no experience needed, just a phone, a small tripod and a dark sky. Where to look, which mode to use on an iPhone, Pixel or Samsung, and how to turn an hour of frames into a timelapse.

item.title: How to Photograph the Milky Way with a Camera
item.description: One wide lens on a tripod, set to manual, pointed at a dark sky. The settings to use, how long the shutter can stay open before stars trail, and how the same frames play back as a timelapse.

item.title: Calibration Frames (Darks, Flats and Biases): The Images That Are Not Photographs
item.description: What calibration frames actually are and what they remove, how to take each one, and why the flats are the ones that catch everybody out. Twenty minutes that decide the picture.

item.title: Siril: From a Folder of Subframes to a Finished Image
item.description: The free, open-source route from raw data to a finished picture. Calibration, stacking, and the one rule about stretching that quietly ruins images when it is broken.

item.title: The ASIAir: Running a Whole Rig From Your Phone
item.description: Plate solving, autofocus, guiding and an unattended imaging plan, all driven from a handset. What the box does, the order a night actually runs in, and where the closed ecosystem bites.
